observations: Two photos show a large open metal container/truck bed filled with multiple car engines/engine assemblies (not one clearly isolated unit).
Engines appear partially disassembled/removed from vehicles; visible cylinder heads, timing/chain areas, and accessory components.
No readable engine model/part number, VIN, or label is visible in the photos.
No clear brand badge (Toyota/Lexus) or model marking is readable on the engines in the photos.

claims.evidence: Photos show multiple engines but no readable RX350/engine code or label.
No readable ES350/engine code or label in photos.
No readable IS250/engine code or label in photos.
No readable Camry/engine code or label in photos.

risks.risk: Wrong engine fitment (seller lists multiple Lexus/Toyota models/years, but photos don’t show the exact engine code).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the engine code/label (e.g., stamped code on engine block or a tag) plus the full engine assembly being sold (one unit) rather than mixed parts.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the worst-case generic used Toyota/Lexus petrol engine with unknown condition/fitment.

risks.risk: Condition unknown: could be incomplete, missing sensors/ECU, or damaged (photos show many parts but not what’s included for one buyer).
risks.proof: Video/clip showing the exact engine unit being picked up, with a checklist of included parts (starter, alternator, intake/exhaust manifolds, sensors, wiring harness, ECU if applicable).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed complete and not guaranteed working.

risks.risk: Not possible to confirm whether it’s one engine or multiple engines being advertised (photos show many engines in the container).
risks.proof: Photo of the specific engine unit with a tag/marker matching the listing, and the same unit shown from start to finish during loading.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the lowest-value scenario: buyer may receive a less complete/less desirable unit.

risks.risk: No proof of running/test (seller text doesn’t include test results; photos can’t confirm).
risks.proof: A short clip of the engine running (or compression/leak-down test sheet) for the exact unit.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code/part number stamped on the block (and any label/tag) for the exact unit being sold.
Confirm what you will receive: is it a complete engine assembly or partial parts? Provide a photo of the exact unit with all included components laid out.
Video clip of the engine being started/running OR compression/leak-down test results for the exact unit.
Photo showing the engine unit marked/identified so it’s not mixed with other engines in the container.
response.reason: The photos show multiple unlabeled engines/assemblies and the seller’s model/year claims can’t be verified remotely because no engine code or identifying label is readable. Without the exact engine identity and condition, a worst-case price cannot be set confidently.
